Class Maps

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.collect.Maps
public final class Maps extends Object
Static factories and collectors for unmodifiable maps that iterate in the order their keys are given.

The map methods behave exactly like their Map.of counterparts, mapOfEntries(Map.Entry...) like Map.ofEntries, mapCopy(Map) like Map.copyOf, and the toMap collectors like Collectors.toUnmodifiableMap, except for iteration order. Map.of and Map.copyOf leave the order unspecified, and it changes from one run to the next. These maps iterate over their keys, values and entries in the order the keys were given. Otherwise they are the same:

  • They are unmodifiable: every mutator method throws UnsupportedOperationException, even when the call would not change the map. That includes the methods of their views and their iterators.
  • They reject null keys and values, and querying them with null, as in get(null) or containsValue(null), throws NullPointerException.
  • The map methods and mapOfEntries(Map.Entry...) reject duplicate keys with IllegalArgumentException, and the toMap collectors without a merger with IllegalStateException.
  • They are serializable if all their keys and values are.
  • They are value-based: do not rely on their identity.
  • equals and hashCode follow the Map contract, so a map from this class equals a Map.of map with the same entries, whatever their order.
Since:
0.1.2

    • mapCopy

      public static <K,V> Map<K,V> mapCopy(Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map)
      Returns an unmodifiable map containing the mappings of map, iterating in the map's iteration order. If map is already a map returned by this class, the copy shares its contents instead of copying them.
      Type Parameters:
      K - the key type
      V - the value type
      Parameters:
      map - the map whose mappings to copy
      Returns:
      a map containing the mappings of map
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if map contains keys that are duplicates according to their equals method, as an IdentityHashMap can
      See Also:
      • Map.copyOf(Map)

    • toMap

      public static <T,K,V> Collector<T,?,Map<K,V>> toMap(Function<? super T, ? extends K> keyMapper, Function<? super T, ? extends V> valueMapper)
      Returns a collector into an unmodifiable map that iterates in encounter order: the ordered counterpart of Collectors.toUnmodifiableMap(Function, Function). If two elements map to the same key, collecting throws IllegalStateException. The resulting map behaves like the other maps of this class.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the input elements
      K - the key type
      V - the value type
      Parameters:
      keyMapper - the function that maps an element to its key
      valueMapper - the function that maps an element to its value
      Returns:
      a collector into an ordered, unmodifiable map

    • toMap

      public static <T,K,V> Collector<T,?,Map<K,V>> toMap(Function<? super T, ? extends K> keyMapper, Function<? super T, ? extends V> valueMapper, BinaryOperator<V> merger)
      Returns a collector into an unmodifiable map that iterates in encounter order: the ordered counterpart of Collectors.toUnmodifiableMap(Function, Function, BinaryOperator). If several elements map to the same key, their values are merged with merger, as Map.merge does, and the key keeps the position of its first element. The resulting map behaves like the other maps of this class.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the input elements
      K - the key type
      V - the value type
      Parameters:
      keyMapper - the function that maps an element to its key
      valueMapper - the function that maps an element to its value
      merger - the function that merges the values of the same key
      Returns:
      a collector into an ordered, unmodifiable map
